Subject: Packaging options — upgrade/downgrade and emergency break-fix coverage

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re narrowing in on a deployment plan but have a few open questions that will drive the procurement path. Two asks up front:

1) BrightWell wants clarity on upgrade/downgrade mechanics — if we move from Metered to Reserved (or back) mid-term, how are credits/proration handled and what are rollback guardrails?

2) For regulated pilots we need a guaranteed break-fix SLA and a path to temporarily spike capacity to handle audits. What does Redwood offer for short-term burst isolation (on our VPC) and does that require a Dedicated contract?

I attached our requirements doc (brightwell_requirements_qa.pdf). Can we put together a short workshop to map packaging choices to procurement options? Prefer week of June 4.

Best,
Lina
Director of Platform, BrightWell Health

Subject: Re: Packaging options — upgrade/downgrade and emergency break-fix coverage

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear list, this is exactly the right level of detail. Short answers up front, then propose a workshop agenda.

1) Upgrade/downgrade mechanics:
- Metered -> Reserved: we can convert usage credits into a pro-rated reserved commitment at the time of conversion. There is a one-time conversion fee (standard) that covers the changeover and any allotment rebalancing.
- Reserved -> Metered: we support mid-term step-downs with a 30-day notice; unused committed credits are convertible to buffered metered credit at a 75% conversion rate to discourage churn.
- Rollback: canary policies let you pin routes to previous model variants for 14 days after a change.

2) Break-fix and spike capacity: short-term isolated burst can be met through our "Burst Capacity Add-on" on hosted or VPC. For guaranteed isolation during audits we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) or a short-term Dedicated pilot (30–90 days). That pilot can be scoped as a "temporary capacity contract" with accelerated onboarding.

Workshop proposal (45 minutes):
- 10m: current BrightWell footprint and audit spike profile (Lina)
- 15m: package matrix (Metered / Reserved / Dedicated) and transition rules (Ben)
- 10m: cost/discount mechanics and conversion scenarios (Jonas)
- 10m: next steps and doc assignation (Rachel)

I attached our latest packaging matrix (redwood_package_matrix_v3.xlsx) and a proposed MOP term sheet for a short Dedicated pilot (proposed_mop_commit_term.docx). Can your procurement team join? Suggested slots: June 5 or June 6 morning PT.

Thanks — I’ll block a preliminary workshop invite for June 5 10am PT unless you tell me a different slot works.

-r
Rachel Kim
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Rachel, Lina — procurement here. A few quick constraints from our side:
- We prefer clear dollar-for-dollar conversions where possible — the 75% conversion on Reserved->Metered will be a hard sell.
- For audit spikes we need the option to pay for a time-bound Dedicated slice without a multi-year commitment (our security team cannot sign long-term without a pilot).
- Any discount must be reflected in the initial SOW; separate discount memos slow procurement review.

Can Ben or Jonas outline a conservative example: 3-month pilot, peak audit window 72 hours with 2x baseline throughput, and the cost/discount impact for (a) Metered with burst add-on, (b) 3-month Dedicated pilot with short-term commit.

Thanks,
Amit
Head of IT Procurement, BrightWell
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Amit Rao <amit.rao@brightwell.ai>, Lina Patel <lina.patel@brightwell.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options — upgrade/downgrade and emergency break-fix coverage

Amit — appreciate the constraints, and totally understand procurement's preference for clarity. Below are two conservative scenarios (back-of-envelope) — final numbers will depend on model mix and sequence lengths.

Scenario A — Metered + Burst Add-on
- Baseline monthly: 1.2M tokens (metered)
- Burst Add-on: 72-hour capacity spike to 2x baseline; priced as time-bound reserved capacity at 1.5x hourly metered rate for the spike window.
- Example cost: Baseline $X, Spike window incremental cost ~ $0.04/token-equivalent (bundled) + one-time setup fee $2,500.
- Discounts: standard early-commit 7% if prepay for 6 months. No conversion credits apply here.

Scenario B — 3-month Dedicated pilot (short-term commit)
- Dedicated slice sized for 2x baseline throughput; contractual term 3 months.
- Cost: Monthly committed fee (includes 24/7 break-fix SLA) + onboarding fee. Example: monthly committed fee replaces metered spend at ~15–25% premium but includes uptime SLA and isolation.
- Discounts: 10% pilot discount applied in SOW. At conversion to a full Reserved contract, we can convert pilot payments to reserved credits at 90% conversion rate.

Notes on downgrade/rollback: for any mid-term downgrades we apply a 30-day notice and convert remaining prepayments per the agreed conversion rate in the SOW. We can negotiate the conversion factor depending on deal size.

I’ve attached a simplified cost sketch in the package matrix and flagged the lines we usually make flexible for pilot customers. If you want, Jonas and I can run a model against your usage export ahead of the call.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
